subject: SIG: hosting matrix & isolation clarifications for procurement

Subject: SIG: hosting and network isolation questions for procurement

Marcus —

Thanks for taking this. Our procurement/security team is completing a SIG (Standardized Information Gathering) assessment and they need clarification on how Redwood's hosting modes differ from a controls and evidence perspective. High level asks: 

- Short matrix showing Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC/on-prem) across tenancy, control plane, KMS, network isolation, audit scope (SOC2), and data residency.
- Example network diagram for each mode (we don't need full docs, just illustrative).
- Which mode removes Redwood from SOC2 scope, if any?

Can you send a short write-up and any artifacts (matrix/diagrams) you can share with procurement by EOD tomorrow? If any items require an NDA/POC, flag them.

Appreciate it —
Sarah Jones
ACME Corp — Security Engineering

Subject: Re: SIG: hosting and network isolation questions for procurement

Sarah —

Thanks for the clear list. I put together a short matrix and an illustrative diagram to help procurement (attached). Key points up front: 

- Hosted (Redwood API): multi-tenant, Redwood-managed control plane and infra. SOC 2 covers Redwood systems; customers rely on contractual commitments and encryption-in-transit + at-rest. KMS: Redwood-managed keys by default; customer-managed KMS available on higher tiers with an agreement. Data residency: regional endpoints available.

- Dedicated (Reserved capacity): single-tenant GPU pools / isolated worker fleet for your account. Control plane and orchestration still operated by Redwood, so those components remain in Redwood's SOC2 scope. Stronger logical isolation, configurable autoscaling policies, and optional customer KMS for keys at rest. Networking: private peering / VPC SR-IOV options; egress controls can be applied.

- Private (VPC / on-prem): control plane can be customer-hosted (Private Control Plane) and on-prem package available. When infrastructure is customer-managed and on-prem, Redwood's SOC2 scope no longer includes that customer infrastructure; Redwood provides the software and configuration guidance. KMS and key custody fully in customer control.

Quick evidence mapping for SIG reviewers (high-level):
- Encryption: TLS certs, in-transit config, and KMS docs (we can share redacted key custody docs).
- Audit logs: per-token tracing, request logs (Hosted/Dedicated: Redwood can export logs; Private: logs are customer-managed).
- Tenant isolation: Dedicated architecture diagram shows isolated worker pools (see diagram).
- SOC2 scope: Hosted & Dedicated components operated by Redwood are covered; Private on-prem is outside Redwood's operational scope.

Attached: hosting_matrix_v1.pdf (matrix + brief notes), redlined_example_network_diagram.png (illustrative).

If procurement needs formal SIG CSV/checkbox answers, we can produce a control_mapping_SIG.xlsx and a slightly expanded architecture_diagram_v2.pdf. Looping in Kimberly for any policy/KMS clarifications.

Best —
Marcus Lin
Senior Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference

Sarah —

Adding a few clarifications on Dedicated vs Private that commonly come up in SIG reviews: 

- Dedicated: offers compute and memory isolation for your workloads (reserved GPU pools). Operational control plane services (scheduling, image registry, telemetry collection) remain Redwood-managed. That means the SOC2 report will include those control plane services. We do offer contractual protections and a right-to-audit path for customers on Dedicated.

- Private (VPC / on-prem): two variants — Private VPC (customer VPC with Redwood components deployed into customer-managed subnets) and On-Prem Install (air-gapped deployables). In both cases, the customer can elect to host the control plane; when they do, the hosted infra falls outside Redwood's operational control and therefore outside our SOC2 boundary.

- KMS options: customer-managed KMS is available for Dedicated and Private. For Dedicated, we typically broker a KMS integration (bring-your-own-key via our connector) — keys are still stored in customer's KMS but some operational metadata lives with Redwood. For Private on-prem, keys never leave customer infrastructure.

Looping in Evelyn to confirm SOC2 boundary language and any standard phrasing procurement expects in SIG answers.

-Kim
Director, Product Security
Redwood Inference

Sarah —

Quick SOC2 scoping summary to include in your SIG response pack: 

- Hosted: Redwood's control plane, orchestration, and worker infrastructure are fully in-scope for Redwood's SOC2 Type II. Customers receive the SOC2 report and we can provide a short attestation letter that describes the hosted service boundary.

- Dedicated: worker fleet and compute are single-tenant but still operated by Redwood; therefore the worker fleet plus the control plane remain in Redwood's SOC2 boundary. We will provide the same SOC2 report and a supplementary note describing the dedicated topology.

- Private (customer-hosted control plane / on-prem): customer-owned infrastructure and operations are out of Redwood's SOC2 scope. Redwood's responsibilities are limited to the software artifacts and configuration guidance we deliver. For SIG purposes, we can provide: architecture_diagram_v2.pdf (annotated scope), control_mapping_SIG.xlsx (per-question references to evidence or owner), and an optional statement of responsibilities (SoR) that procurement can include in their vendor assessment.

Next steps: 
1) Marcus/Kim will upload the two additional artifacts (architecture_diagram_v2.pdf, control_mapping_SIG.xlsx) to the shared drive link and mark any items that require an NDA.
2) Procurement: tell us which SIG sections you need completed first (networking, cryptography, access control) and we'll prioritize.

Happy to jump on a 30-min call if that helps close the SIG quickly.

Regards,
Evelyn Hart
Head, Compliance & Privacy
Redwood Inference
